title: CmdPal JS/TS Extensions - Phase 2: JSON-RPC transport + manifest
summary: The refreshed stacked review found five current robustness issues: the notification channel reader contract, bare-CR stderr framing, unbounded inbound frames, unbounded request concurrency, and fail-open manifest containment races.

status.label: Review comments ready
status.detail: Five general review notes are pinned to the refreshed upstream head.

next_action: Review and selectively post the drafted request-changes comments.

proposed_comments.title: Keep notification queue reads safe under producer pressure
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep notification queue reads safe under producer pressure

**Severity:** `high`

The bounded notification queue removes the oldest item from a producer path while the consumer is also reading. Configure the channel for multiple readers, or move eviction behind the sole consumer, so the declared channel contract matches the actual concurrent access pattern.

proposed_comments.title: Treat standalone carriage returns as stderr line terminators
proposed_comments.body:
### Treat standalone carriage returns as stderr line terminators

**Severity:** `medium`

A bare `\r` must emit and reset the current stderr line. Otherwise progress-style output is concatenated into one record and can consume the line and volume budgets unexpectedly.

proposed_comments.title: Bound inbound JSON-RPC frames before allocation
proposed_comments.body:
### Bound inbound JSON-RPC frames before allocation

**Severity:** `high`

Reject oversized `Content-Length` declarations and oversized headers before allocating the payload buffer. The transport must not allow an extension to make the host buffer an unbounded or multi-gigabyte inbound message.

proposed_comments.title: Apply bounded admission control to inbound requests
proposed_comments.body:
### Apply bounded admission control to inbound requests

**Severity:** `high`

With a null synchronization context, inbound requests can execute concurrently. Gate request dispatch with a finite capacity and return the defined `ServerBusy` error when that capacity is exhausted, while retaining enough capacity for reentrant callbacks.

proposed_comments.title: Fail closed when a manifest path segment disappears
proposed_comments.body:
### Fail closed when a manifest path segment disappears

**Severity:** `high`

If a file or directory disappears between existence and attribute checks, treat the segment as untrusted rather than as a confirmed non-reparse point. Containment validation must not succeed without successfully validating every path segment.

review.body: The refreshed implementation should fail closed and remain bounded under malformed or adversarial extension traffic.

judgment.rationale: The refreshed transport and manifest implementation still has concurrency-contract, framing, allocation-bound, admission-control, and path-validation failures that were reproduced and fixed on the reconciled fork branch.
evidence: The producer path calls Reader.TryRead while the consumer also reads a channel declared for a single reader.
The stderr parser discards standalone carriage returns without emitting or resetting the buffered line.
The header-delimited JSON-RPC handler lacks application-level header and payload bounds before allocation.
Inbound dispatch can execute concurrently while the defined ServerBusy error remains unused.
A missing path segment after an existence check is treated as a trusted non-reparse result.
All five prior Copilot threads were replied to and resolved; the final audit found no new published findings.
The reconciled x64 Debug ViewModels build passed, and the focused pre-reconciliation run passed 168 tests.
judgment.recommended_action: After explicit maintainer approval and a current-head freshness check, post the selected notes as a request-changes review.
